chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran said:

I asked Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him) about Divine Unity (Tawhid), so I said: 'Is He presumed to be a thing?' He replied: 'Yes, [He is] Incomprehensible and Unlimited. Whatever your imagination conceives of Him as, that is contrary to Him. Nothing resembles Him, and imagination does not perceive Him. How could imagination perceive Him when He is beyond what is rationally understood and beyond what is conceived in imagination? He is merely a Thing that is Incomprehensible and Unlimited.'
ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq define God as a 'Thing' while remaining beyond human imagination?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the apparent paradox of God being a 'Thing' (*shay'*) by distinguishing between conceptual existence and sensory limitation, affirming He is 'non-conceptualizable and unlimited.' This aligns with the Shia theological principle of *Tanzih* (transcendence), where any human imagination or attribute is necessarily finite and thus contrary to the Infinite Divine Essence. The narration emphasizes that while God exists, He is beyond the reach of *wahm* (imaginative conception), ensuring His uniqueness (*fard*) is preserved against anthropomorphism.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 6. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan alSaffar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Isa ibn `Ubayd, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abu Najran

that I asked Abu Ja`far the Second (AS) about Divine Unity [Tawhid], so I said: “Is He presumed to be a thing?” Consequently, he (AS) replied: Yes. However, since He is Incomprehensible, and Unlimited, He is unlike anything you can conceive. Nothing resembles Him. Imagination perceives Him not. And how could imagination perceive Him when He is beyond all imagination? He is an Imagined Thing which is Incomprehensible and Unlimited.
